climb.rationale: Index of coincidence first, then the published n-gram counts, which is the ordering Ostwald and Weierud describe. Measured at 167 letters with ten pairs: n-grams alone from the identity plugboard recover the exact plugboard on 3 of 8 key draws; seeding with an index-of-coincidence climb recovers 8 of 8 for 1.6x the work.
climb.window_rationale: Fixed at W = 117 by the sweep rule preregistered in phase1-windowed-climb-power-v1 before that run, whose three deciding predictions held. W = 134 measured slightly higher on indel draws there; the rule forbids choosing it on that evidence.

positive_controls.rationale: The five independently solved 1941 Army plaintexts Phase 7 already uses, each kept as its own message with its own indicator and enciphered by enigma.EnigmaI under one shared ten-pair daily key. That is the real Army situation: several short messages under one key. An earlier version of this control concatenated the five into two messages at the target lengths and failed, because the junctions between unrelated messages are n-grams no Army text contains; the concatenated form was not a legitimate control and was replaced rather than reinterpreted.

key.plugboard: AV BS CG DL FU HZ IN KM OW RX

positive_controls.rationale: Three messages at exactly the target lengths 167, 107 and 97, from constructed Army-style text that cannot overlap the published n-gram counts. Trades authenticity for a guarantee of no training overlap, so the two controls fail in different ways if either weakness matters.

key.plugboard: AN BY CF DR GJ HS IL KM PV QZ

limitations: The controls are constructed or independently solved plaintexts, not authentic held-out Army traffic with an authentic daily key.

The messages behind the published 1941 n-gram counts are not enumerated, so overlap between the authentic control plaintexts and the scorer's training data cannot be ruled out. The constructed control exists to bound that risk, not to remove it.

The positive controls are body-direct and are handed the true wheel order, ring setting and start positions. They certify the stecker stage at the target lengths and say nothing about the rotor enumeration, which the sweeps and calibrations cover separately.

Every result assumes UKW-B, the Army/Air Force wheels I-V and the 1940+ clear-Grundstellung indicator procedure. A different reflector, a Naval wheel or a different indicator convention is outside every space searched here.
The calibrations use one plaintext per cell and a single key draw per cell. They locate the detection boundary to within a cell, not to a precise length.

The authentic control pools five short messages under one daily key (275 letters); the constructed control pools three at the target lengths (371 letters). Neither certifies a single 167-letter message on its own, which is what the capability calibration measures.

The middle-complete space has an exact equivalent for every daily key at 167 letters (rule_key_coverage 1.0). A key is still found only if the climb converges at one of its equivalents and scores into the top 100 of nine times as many settings as v3 searched; the stated power measures the first on planted draws and stands in for the second with a pooled null.

The companion calibration (phase1-companion-calibration-v1) was measured with middle-past-notch candidates. Under middle_complete a candidate's middle ring can put the notch inside a companion, and the companion check presents the candidate's rings as reported, so a companion whose true left wheel steps at a different letter is deciphered exactly only up to that letter. The joint figure in refuted_by includes that case at its natural rate on planted draws.
No result here is an accepted break: a confirmed candidate's plaintext still has to be read and reviewed before accepted_break could change.

The stated power is measured on planted single-indel and clean 167-letter draws through the complete rule's parameterization in the planted key's neighbourhood (phase1-middle-complete-power-v1), judged by a 6-sigma threshold over a pooled wrong-setting null. Under a normal null the top-100 retention cutoff over 246.8 million settings is about 4.9 sigma, below that threshold, but v2's and v3's maxima sat about 0.7 sigma above the normal expectation over 27.4 million, so the null's far tail is heavier than normal and the real cutoff is not measured. The joint companion figure was measured post hoc and preregistered nowhere.

The sweep scores each setting by the better of two 117-letter windows, so its scores are not on the scale of v2's whole-message scores; the indicator confirmation, which compares a pooled date score with the candidate's own sweep score, is reported but is even less informative here than in v2. The companion check alone decides.
A candidate found through the tail window is reported at the setting that deciphers the tail, which for a garbled message is one keystroke away from the setting of the head.

The power is conditional on v2 and v3 both null, with 'missed by both past-notch arms' on planted draws standing in for both sweeps being null, the same stand-in and the same limits as phase1-middle-complete-power-v1: one plaintext, a single indel only, 400 draws per cell, and strata of 57, 118 and 74 draws.

The prior q of one dropped or inserted letter is unmeasured. q = 0.2 is the value phase1-middle-complete-power-v1 declared; the stated power at other q is given in refuted_by so another belief can be applied without a rerun.

The cited paper (Sullivan and Weierud 2005, footnote 42) places Batch C on a different radio network and its authors suspect differently wired wheels. Every figure here assumes wheels I-V as wired; if that is wrong the power is zero and a null says nothing about these messages.

phase1-split-point-power-v1's yield model favoured a split-point sweep per host-hour at every prior (0.0059 against 0.0030 at q = 0.2) but its rule did not consult the yield model once S1 and S2 were both refuted. This sweep follows the rule as written; it is the more powerful single sweep, not the more efficient one.
hypothesis: BYQMZ, FKQLZ and XFEDT of 1941-09-30 are Enigma I traffic (UKW-B, wheels I-V, ten stecker pairs) under one daily key, and BYQMZ's key is one both completed middle-past-notch sweeps (v2, whole message; v3, W = 117) could miss, most plausibly because it has no exact equivalent in the past-notch space (its middle wheel's notch falls inside the message), with or without one dropped or inserted letter. A complete sweep of the middle-complete space on BYQMZ (246,767,040 settings: every wheel order, left and middle offset, right position and right ring, at the middle start just past the notch and at the eight from which the notch falls inside 167 letters) with v3's W = 117 head-and-tail climb then retains at least one candidate that the companion-body confirmation accepts: FKQLZ and XFEDT each deciphered at all 17,576 starts under the candidate's wheel order, rings and plugboard, both best starts at z >= 6.
refuted_by: No retained candidate companion-confirmed. Stated power, fixed by the preregistered rule of phase1-split-point-power-v1 as the complete rule's measured conditional rate: among planted draws both past-notch climbs miss (phase1-middle-complete-power-v1), the complete rule with the W = 117 climb detects 34 of 57 clean (59.6%) and 57 of 192 with one indel (29.7%: 24 of 118 with the indel in letters 56-111, 33 of 74 elsewhere), 0.460 at a prior q = 0.2 of one dropped or inserted letter. Detection and companion confirmation measured jointly on the same draws (artifacts/phase1-joint-power-v3-middle-complete-w117.json, post hoc, preregistered nowhere): 33 of 57 clean (57.9%) and 55 of 192 with one indel (28.6%), 0.445 at q = 0.2 (0.535 at q = 0.05, 0.353 at q = 0.5). Given v2 and v3 null, a null here multiplies the remaining odds of a standard Enigma I reading by about 0.56 at q = 0.2: a moderate test, not a decisive one. A middle-third indel stays largely invisible (23 of 118 jointly), and nothing here tests two faults, other reflectors, other wheel wirings, Naval wheels, other indicator procedures or non-Enigma systems.

body_direct_sweep.rationale: Chosen by the preregistered decision rule of phase1-split-point-power-v1, whose deciding predictions S1 and S2 were both refuted on 2026-10-07: the split-point climb is dropped and the complete-rule sweep is preregistered with its measured conditional rate as its stated power. Same message, climb (W = 117, batched engine), retention, start axes, right-ring axis, companions and threshold as v3; only the ring rule changes, from middle_past_notch to middle_complete, which multiplies the settings by nine. The space contains v3's 27,418,560 settings exactly; they are swept again rather than skipped, so that the sweep is the arm phase1-middle-complete-power-v1 measured and its score distribution covers the whole space. Projected cost at v3's measured 2.22 ms per setting on 10 workers: about 152 hours (6.3 days) on an idle host. Each of the 1,560 checkpointed chunks holds 158,184 settings, about an hour of one worker, so a stop loses at most that much per worker.

predictions.statement: At least one of the 100 retained candidates is companion-confirmed (min over FKQLZ and XFEDT of best-start z >= 6).
If a candidate is confirmed, it is also the sweep's rank-1 candidate on BYQMZ alone.

If a candidate is confirmed, its setting is not one v3 swept: its middle start is one of the eight the complete rule adds. v3's settings are a subset of this space, and the climb and the companion check are deterministic, so a confirmed setting v3 had swept would have been retained and confirmed by v3.

Every retained candidate at a setting v3 also swept is one v3 retained, at the same wheel order, rings and start, with the same plugboard and a score per letter within 1e-6 of v3's. A failure means the climb changed between 7ae72f8 and this run.

If no candidate is confirmed, the sweep's top score lies between z = 5.5 and z = 7.5 over the distribution of all 246,767,040 settings' scores (v2 6.03 and v3 6.22 over 27.4 million; a normal tail adds about 0.4 for nine times as many settings), i.e. at the noise maximum.

status: preregistered 2026-10-07; engine amended to cuda 2026-10-08 before the GPU run (see amendments)

amendments.change: climb.engine from 'batched' to 'cuda'. Nothing else changes: message, space, ring rule, climb (phases, pair limit, passes, gain, W = 117), retention, companions, threshold, predictions and stated power are as preregistered.
amendments.decided_by: the maintainer, after the CUDA engine's build and benchmark (docs/phase1-experiment-history.md, 'CUDA climb engine: build and benchmark (2026-10-08)')
amendments.disclosure: A deviation from the preregistered engine, disclosed here and in the history before the GPU run. A CPU run of this configuration with engine 'batched' started 2026-10-07 23:28:24 UTC from 31dfbcc and had finished 200 of 1,560 chunks when this amendment was made; the engine is part of the checkpoint fingerprint, so the GPU run starts from zero and does not read that checkpoint.
amendments.why_no_number_changes: The cuda engine reproduces the batched climb bit for bit: 150 of 150 v4 chunks recomputed from a copy of the CPU checkpoint gave byte-identical records (23,727,600 settings), as did 4,000 random climbs and v4's preflight samples. Its preflight check against the batched climber must pass before any target search. Every chunk the CPU run finished is to be compared with the GPU run's record for the same chunk, and any difference voids the GPU result.
amendments.cost: 0.00741 ms per setting on the RTX 3090, about 0.5 hours for the 246,767,040 settings, against about 152 hours on 10 CPU workers.

pre_run_facts.disclosure: Everything below was known before this run and shaped this configuration. None of it is a result of this sweep.
pre_run_facts.choice: phase1-split-point-power-v1 refuted S1 (52 of 118 against 54 needed) and S2 (18 of 74 against 23 needed) on 2026-10-07, and its rule chose this sweep. The maintainer delegated the choice between the rule and the yield model; this configuration follows the rule.
pre_run_facts.joint_power: artifacts/phase1-joint-power-v3-middle-complete-w117.json was measured after that result and before this configuration was committed, by scripts/joint_power.py unchanged, from a clean tree at 6dc6611. Its detection flags match the control's complete_w117 arm on all 800 draws.
pre_run_facts.smoke_run: A 108-setting run of this rule through the runner (wheel order I-II-III, one left start, two middle starts, three right positions, two right rings, keep 5; output in a scratch directory, not committed) passed the preflight and both positive controls, swept 9 settings per start and right ring, and on a second invocation resumed both chunks from its checkpoint with identical candidates and score distribution.

run_constraint: Amended 2026-10-08: the cuda engine ignores --jobs and needs nvcc and a CUDA device; the preregistered text follows. Not run. Run from a clean tree with --jobs 10 after this configuration is committed and merged, on a host that is otherwise idle, since it occupies ten cores for about a week. The checkpoint under build/ (git-ignored; do not clean it while the sweep is unfinished) lets it be stopped and resumed by rerunning the same command. A resumed run repeats the preflight, the positive controls and both confirmations, and its artifact's timing fields cover only the last invocation, so record every start, stop and resume in the history.
